The rule now covers any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock`, but I could not run the regex checks. The Bash tool stopped asking for approval partway through, and my last two attempts to run a quick regex check were refused, as was a `git diff`.

**What changed:** in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, the two mock rules in `addTestConventions()` (`.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`) are replaced by one rule:

```java
testFilesConventions.add(new Convention(".*[/\\\\](__)?mock[^/\\\\]*[/\\\\].*", "", "Mock resources"));
```

- The folder name must begin with `mock` or `__mock`, and `[^/\\]*` lets the rest be anything: punctuation, non-ASCII, or nothing at all.
- Both `/` and `\` count as separators, so Windows paths match.
- The match stays within one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/`, and `src/main/java/` do not match, and neither do `mock.java` or `mockery.java`.
- The existing `mocks/` rule and the other folders you listed (`__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`) still match.

**Verification:** `mvn -q -o compile` on the `codeanalyzer` module succeeds. I did not run any tests, because the module has no existing tests for this class and I did not add one. I checked the regex by reading it against your cases, not by executing it, so a quick run of the cases would be worth doing. The cases to run are the elasticsearch `mock/` path, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`, and the backslash variants, plus the negatives listed above.

I did not commit anything.
